title: Configured arguments are interpolated into shell code without quoting
reasoning: The command is executed as shell text, but only the prompt is quoted. The configured binary, model, and extra_args are joined verbatim. Arguments containing spaces lose their boundaries, and shell metacharacters or command substitutions execute as code in the agent runtime. Exploitability depends on who controls configuration; ordinary arguments containing whitespace already cause incorrect execution.
reproduction: Configure an extra argument containing a literal command substitution, such as --example=$(printf injected). The generated shell command evaluates the substitution instead of passing the configured argument literally.
recommendation: Build a literal argv list and apply shlex.join to the entire invocation. Keep the fixed PATH export separate from the quoted invocation, or pass PATH through the runtime environment.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were supplied or linked for this feature, so argument-boundary and shell-literal coverage cannot be verified.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test that binary paths, model values, and extra arguments containing whitespace, quotes, dollar signs, and shell metacharacters reach a test executable unchanged and cause no shell side effects.
